en.name: Valentine of Rome
en.summary: Third-century Roman priest and martyr whose feast day became associated with romantic love through later medieval tradition.
en.body: Very little can be established with historical certainty about Valentine beyond that he was a priest, or possibly a bishop, martyred near Rome in the third century, likely during the persecution under Emperor Claudius II, and that early Christians venerated his memory enough to build a basilica over his burial place on the Via Flaminia. The romantic associations that make him globally famous today emerged only much later, in medieval Europe, when poets including Chaucer linked his February feast day to the springtime mating season of birds, and popular legend added details, unverifiable historically, such as a story of him secretly marrying Christian couples in defiance of an imperial ban, or restoring the sight of a jailer's daughter and signing a farewell note "from your Valentine." Whatever the historical facts of his martyrdom, his feast day evolved over centuries into the global celebration of romantic love observed today.
